firstMismatch.cEntry: invent.c:getobj splits the requested count; wield.c:dowield finishes the split child and continues through wielding
firstMismatch.jsEntry: js/invent.js:getobj creates the split child, then js/wield.js:dowield refuses that child with UnsupportedWieldError

summary: The admitted case types #wield, selects count 2, then selects inventory item a. C invent.c:getobj splits the requested count; wield.c:dowield recognizes the child, assigns it its own inventory slot with finish_splitting, and continues through ready_weapon. JS now follows the same path, including restoration and the already-wielded result when the split parent is the current weapon. The complete replay matches all 168 screens, RNG calls, and cursor positions.

source.branch: Read wield.c:dowield() in full (354-457). After getobj returns the counted split child, C first handles the welded-primary refusal and unsplits the child. Otherwise it checks whether the primary weapon is the split parent; if so it unsplits, sets wep to uwep, and follows already_wielded. For any other child it calls finish_splitting and jumps to wielding. JS now preserves this ordering and both counted-child outcomes.
callers: cmd.c dispatches the #wield extended command to wield.c:dowield; js/cmd.js dispatches the recorded wield command to js/wield.js:dowield.

wield.c:dowield calls invent.c:getobj with GETOBJ_PROMPT | GETOBJ_ALLOWCNT. invent.c:getobj splits the selected count and returns the child; wield.c:dowield calls finish_splitting before ready_weapon.
dependencies: invent.c:getobj supplies the counted child and split context.
wield.c:finish_splitting assigns the child a distinct inventory letter; its JS helper was introduced in accepted quiver delivery 2b4144ab4a6e473970b0a53cae76110c80a07d76.
wield.c:ready_weapon performs the ordinary weapon setup after the counted branch.

evidence: The published v74 admission evaluation at source base 8f280fd706dcfdad7c302cc39301cb056753af10 records 118/168 screens, 2684/2690 RNG calls, and 118/168 cursors, with null error.

The admitted recording reaches #wield at segment 0 step 116, selects count 2 at step 117, and selects inventory item a at step 118. The first mismatch was the unsupported objsplit child branch in wield.c:dowield.

C wield.c:dowield (354-457) finishes a counted child before jumping to wielding, except when its parent is already wielded or the current primary weapon is welded. The JavaScript branch now unsplits the already-wielded parent and welded-refusal cases, and gives other counted children their own inventory slot before ready_weapon.

Focused source-pinned tests drive the real getobj count queue through dowield, assert that two of five arrows become the wielded child while three remain in the parent, and verify the already-wielded parent is restored with C’s refusal result.

Post-fix replay at source commit d043bf8db515b7d9df362307023eba82447467bf matches the complete admitted segment: 168/168 screens, 2690/2690 RNG calls, 168/168 cursors, and the input boundary; no unported calls remain.
